risk_if_not_implemented: Without Digital Media Sanitization Documentation, sensitive and/or regulated data may be retained beyond authorized periods or recovered from improperly disposed media and equipment. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data (R-AM-3), Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Secure Disposal, Destruction or Re-Use of Equipment
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy or repurpose technology assets using organization-defined techniques and methods to prevent:
(1) Data recovery; and
(2) Components from being resold, redistributed and/or reused through unauthorized channels.
compensating_control_1.justification: Secure Disposal, Destruction or Re-Use of Equipment (AST-22) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of System Media Sanitization Documentation (DCH-18.2) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Data applicability. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy and/or erase digital and non-digital media when it is no longer required, using organization-defined procedures.
compensating_control_2.justification: Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal (DCH-17) provides physical access control that compensates for the absence of System Media Sanitization Documentation (DCH-18.2) by preventing unauthorized physical interaction with systems and infrastructure. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
